newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy seen buying marks for lire -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy seen buying marks for lire -dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Italy was buying marks for lire at just under 972 per mark, Milan foreign exchange dealers said.
At 1055 GMT, the lira was quoted at 972.08/2.28 per mark after a day's high of 970.65.
"There's a bit of nervousness on the market," one dealer said. "There's talk of intervention by central banks selling dollars and of supporting the mark against European currencies."
Dealers said the Italian central bank was keeping a close eye on the appreciating lira, intervening with mark purchases just below the 972 area.
"Consequently the cross is steady, it's not going down but it has no intention of rising either," one dealer said.
